cases.description: Posted and reversed journals form the posted ledger: the corrected purchase counts once at its new amount; transfers, the card repayment and the reimbursable expense are neither income nor expenses; the refund reduces August spending; pending and draft entries are excluded.
A July to June financial year has twelve monthly rows, empty months included.
Net spending per expense category, largest first; refunds reduce the category and splits count towards each category.
Net spending per payee; entries without a payee share the empty key labelled No payee, and a reversal keeps its original's payee.
Balances as the user reads them on a date (a liability's owed amount is positive), in chart order, with every journal that touched the account.
Without a date every posted journal counts; pending and draft entries never do.

Net worth at each month end (the range end for a partial month) starts from the balance before the range, excludes accounts left out of net worth and includes the reimbursement receivable, so lending money does not reduce it.
A calendar year has twelve month-end points.
Transfers within the account set are internal; a transfer to an account outside it crosses the boundary; the net row lists the boundary-crossing journals in date order.
